extracted.intended_audience: companies, investors, cities, policymakers and general readers interested in environmental disclosure
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria used by the Carbon Disclosure Project (CDP) for corporate, city, supplier and commodity-level environmental disclosure and scoring; includes CDP programs (climate, water, forests, supply chain, cities) and the investor-led Carbon Action requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: CDP scoring framework (disclosure → awareness → management → leadership)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scores are calculated according to a standardized method which measures whether and how well a company responds to each question. A company goes through four main steps, starting with disclosure of their current position, moving to awareness which looks at whether a company is conscious of its environmental impact, to management, and finally leadership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High CDP score (A-list) indicates environmental awareness, advanced sustainability governance and leadership to address climate change. Scoring is question-by-question and follows the four-step progression from disclosure to leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carbon Action initiative — three investor-requested company actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Over 300 investors with US$25 trillion in assets under management ask the world's highest emitting companies to take three specific actions in response to climate change: Make emissions reductions (year-on-year); Publicly disclose emission reduction targets; Make ROI-positive investments in projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carbon Action is investor-led and intended to show how companies in investment portfolios are managing carbon emissions and energy efficiency; companies' adoption of these three actions is the basis for investor engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climate change program — disclosure of climate risks and low-carbon opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: CDP's climate change program aims to reduce companies' greenhouse gas emissions and mitigate climate change risk. CDP requests information on climate risks and low carbon opportunities from the world's largest companies on behalf of over 800 institutional investor signatories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies are expected to report on both risks and opportunities related to climate change; the program frames disclosure as a tool to drive emissions reductions and inform investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Water program — disclosure and reduction of water-related impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: The program motivates companies to disclose and reduce their environmental impacts by using the power of investors and companies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies are asked to disclose water-related risks and management approaches; the program leverages investor pressure to encourage reduction of water impacts (no detailed questionnaire text provided on this page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply chain program — supplier disclosure of climate and water approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2016, some 90 organisations, representing over US$2.5 trillion of purchasing power, requested that their suppliers disclose information on how they are approaching climate and water risks and opportunities. Data was gathered from over 4,000 suppliers worldwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The criterion is that suppliers report their approach to climate and water risks/opportunities; CDP reports aggregate outcomes (e.g., reported over US$12 billion worth of savings from emission reduction activities) as evidence of impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forests program — disclosure on commodities driving deforestation
rubrics_metrics.description: CDP's forests program collects information about the four agricultural commodities responsible for most deforestation: timber, palm oil, cattle and soy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program targets corporate disclosure on sourcing and impacts related to these commodities; it has a network of signatory investors (over 290) representing significant assets to encourage disclosure and improved practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cities program — annual measurement and public disclosure of city GHG emissions via questionnaire
rubrics_metrics.description: CDP Cities provides a platform for cities to measure, manage and disclose their environmental data. More than 500 cities currently measure and disclose environmental data annually via the platform of CDP Cities, based upon a simple questionnaire that allows city governments to disclose their greenhouse gas emission data publicly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cities are expected to complete the CDP Cities questionnaire annually, enabling public disclosure of GHG emissions and facilitating measurement and management of emissions at the municipal level.
